findings.title: Trusted side-panel WebMCP calls bypass target-site automation authorization
findings.status: Existing defect persists; worker forwarding reproduced
findings.trigger: A legitimate extension page dispatches WEBMCP_CALL_TOOL to an unapproved target tab (or an origin whose browser automation grant was revoked).
findings.impact: The background forwards a site tool request despite target origin not being in the allowlist/browser-control consent. The content listener can dispatch the call on that page. A trusted sender is being used as authority over the destination.
proof: Real registered background onMessage handler accepted a trusted panel request for https://unapproved.example/form while the allowlist and browser-control consent only contained https://site-a.example. Actual diagnostic object was {success:true,forwardCount:1}; required was {success:false,forwardCount:0}.
WEBMCP_CALL_TOOL resolves a tab and immediately forwards. The generic forwarder does not check site policy. Trusted extension-page sender authorization does not inspect destination origin.

content.ts computes originApproved during initialization, but handleMessage does not await it or a fresh policy decision before handleMessageAsync. The WEBMCP cases dispatch their site tool handlers directly.
findings.minimal_test: Dispatch both WEBMCP_DISCOVER_TOOLS and WEBMCP_CALL_TOOL from a trusted panel to an unapproved/revoked target. Require denial before tabs.sendMessage; positive approved case must succeed. Independently invoke the real content listener after policy revocation and require denial before site handlers. Retain direct-tool side-effect approval requirements.
findings.validation_test: rejects WebMCP calls targeting an unapproved tab despite a trusted panel sender
findings.limits: The real worker forwarding decision is exercised. tabs.sendMessage is a transport mock returning success; no live content script or page tool action was executed. The content authorization omission is independently source-traced.

findings.title: Stop reports cancellation success after the cloud cancellation API refuses it
findings.status: Real worker decision reproduced; mounted panel and durable lifecycle source-traced
findings.trigger: Press Stop for a known owned cloud run while cancellation returns server/network/rate-limit error.
findings.impact: The panel marks the answer no longer streaming and can send the next queued follow-up while the durable task may continue. The worker emits Cancelled before the API result and then returns success even when cancellation failed.
proof: Real registered CANCEL_STREAM handler invoked the cancellation seam once, received {status:error,code:server_error,message:Cancellation service unavailable}, logged that failure, but returned response.success=true. The expectation success=false failed.
The worker broadcasts a done:true/error:Cancelled chunk before requesting server cancellation, logs failure without returning it, and always returns success.

The mounted requestStreamCancellation discards the worker response and swallows rejection. cancelCurrentManagedStream clears streaming/current stream immediately and invokes sendNextFollowUp in finally.

The server cancellation owner updates cloud_agent_runs.cancellation_requested_at. Its workflow is started independently of the browser request and its invocation owns the AbortController, checking the persisted flag; aborting a follower cannot substitute for this write.
findings.minimal_test: Mount the panel with a recovered owned durable run, click Stop, inject cancellation rejection, and require a visible unconfirmed/failure state with no falsely cancelled chunk or automatic next dependent turn. A successful cancellation should poll a confirmed terminal state. Include a server workflow fixture that remains running until the cancellation flag changes.
findings.validation_test: returns a cancellation failure instead of reporting success when the server refused Stop
findings.limits: The real worker return value and cancellation invocation are reproduced; provider/API transport is mocked. Continued live tool execution or billing is not observed and is a conditional impact supported by the independently traced server-owned lifecycle.

findings.title: Approved WebMCP form checkbox arguments are submitted with the wrong state
findings.status: Existing defect persists; real DOM fallback reproduced
findings.trigger: Approve a DOM-backed site tool whose form has a checkbox, passing its advertised boolean argument true.
findings.impact: The call returns submitted:true although checked remains false, so submitted data does not match what the user approved. Related radio/select/unmatched-field cases remain unverified in this probe.
proof: The real callTool path approved through window.confirm and invoked the real callToolViaDom on a jsdom checkbox form. The requestSubmit seam was invoked once and result.success was true, but checkbox.checked remained false.
callToolViaDom assigns String(value) to .value for all fields, ignoring the checked property. Its form schema discovery advertises checkbox booleans.
findings.minimal_test: Use real checkbox/radio/select forms. Assert checked/selected values and events before a captured requestSubmit, and reject unmatched or invalid arguments before submission. Include approved and refused paths.
findings.validation_test: applies approved boolean form arguments before claiming WebMCP submission succeeded
findings.limits: Real DOM mutation path is exercised in jsdom with requestSubmit captured and confirm approved; no external form was submitted.

findings.title: Closing an AGI Work panel explicitly cancels its durable cloud task
findings.status: Cancellation decision reproduced; durable-work product disposition required
findings.known_flaw_id_match: Continuity class candidate; existing row is generic/stale and needs root disposition rather than duplicate registration.
findings.trigger: Submit an AGI Work task, receive its running cloud run reference, then close/disconnect the side-panel keepalive port.
findings.impact: The worker aborts the local follower and requests cancellation of the durable server run. The restart/resume machinery cannot preserve work that this path deliberately cancels.
proof: The real registered runtime handler accepted CHAT_MESSAGE with workMode:agiwork; the mocked provider emitted a cloud run reference through the real onRunReference callback and waited for the actual request signal. Invoking the real registered port onDisconnect caused the server-cancel seam to be called once with that run.
Every active stream matching the client instance is cancelled/deleted on disconnect. ActiveChatStream retains no workMode/detach policy distinction.
The panel has stored-run reopen recovery and live-port resume code, and the request forwards AGI Work mode, but the keepalive owner does not preserve durable work across follower close.
findings.minimal_test: Run a durable AGI Work fixture independently of the panel, close the follower, reopen and recover the same run. Require server cancellation only for an explicit Stop/owner revocation if background completion is the intended contract; retain ordinary chat shutdown policy separately.
findings.validation_test: detaches a durable AGI Work follower when its panel closes without cancelling the task
findings.limits: The real worker cancellation decision is exercised; provider stream and cancel API are seams. Treat this as a demonstrated behavior and policy-contingent gap until root confirms intended AGI Work background-completion contract. It is not claimed to be a live browser suspension experiment.

findings.title: A new login session for the same account hides retained Chrome history
findings.status: Real history persistence/filtering reproduced; Clerk owner and mounted history source-traced
findings.trigger: Save a Chrome conversation, sign out, then sign in to the same Clerk account with a new session id.
findings.impact: The history drawer and active conversation lookup cannot find the retained record. Pending local mirror work is also filtered out. This hides data rather than deleting it; account-backed history cannot be rehydrated by the current flags-only pull.
proof: The real upsertConversation/listConversations/getConversation functions ran against callback-correct mocked chrome.storage.local. Old-session owner could list/read the chat, another account saw none, and the persisted conversations array retained one record. The same account/new-session list returned [] instead of one chat.
Clerk resolveSessionOwner sets authIncarnation to session.id. Persistent conversation owner is that complete ManagedCloudOwner, and sameManagedCloudOwner compares both accountId and authIncarnation.

The mounted owner-transition resets visible messages/conversation id and drawer calls listConversations for the current owner. Cloud delta pull filters the same owner and its insert port is a no-op, so it cannot recover earlier-session history.
findings.minimal_test: Save account A history under session A1, revoke/sign out, sign in as A2 and require retained history plus safe pending mirror recovery; account B remains isolated. Model persistent data ownership separately from auth-incarnation operation leases, retaining strict stale-stream/approval/cancellation fencing.
findings.validation_test: retains account-owned history when the same account signs in with a new Clerk session
findings.limits: Real persistence normalization/filtering is tested with callback Chrome storage mocks. Real Clerk login and whole panel rendering are not mounted. Changing session authority comparison globally would weaken the correctly strict in-flight ownership boundary and is not the proposed fix.

observations.title: The managed turn path has genuine ownership and recovery machinery
observations.detail: Owner validation, captured credentials, client-instance plus stream keys, active conversation restore fencing, run-reference persistence and replay primitives are implemented. Their existence is not end-to-end success evidence for panel closure or auth-session replacement.

observations.title: Current Chrome cloud conversation mirroring is outbound plus flags/deletion pull
observations.detail: Pull only patches pin/archive flags or deletes known local bindings; insertion is a no-op and does not hydrate message bodies. Opening a cloud project conversation explicitly opens web chat in a new tab. Definition prose contains both local-authoritative browser ownership and broader canonical cloud continuity; root should resolve the actual contract before counting this as missing in-panel cross-surface continuity.

observations.title: Native context handoff has explicit confirmation and authenticated envelope enforcement
observations.detail: Preview confirmation, expiry, HMAC authenticated host session and captured-current-session checks are present. The VS Code affordance is a URI anchor and not a proven dead control. Pairing handshake/host verifier were not fully independently audited.

observations.title: Source-only worker lifecycle tests cannot establish browser lifecycle outcomes
observations.detail: These tests match source fragments. Their comment says the large worker cannot be imported without a full Chrome surface; the real-worker harness used here successfully imports it with explicit API seams. Source regex tests do not exercise real port closure, worker death or reattach journeys.
